editorial.meta_description: The Associate, Accredited Pension Administrator designation from LOMA is officially retired as of 2015-12-31 with no successor program available for any
editorial.overview: The Associate, Accredited Pension Administrator (AAPA) designation was a professional certification program formerly offered by LOMA. It covered topics including annuity products, contract administration, tax and regulatory considerations, and customer service operations. This exam is officially retired as of 2015-12-31. LOMA does not provide a successor designation for this program. Candidates seeking current professional credentials should consult LOMA directly for information regarding their active certification offerings and updated educational requirements for industry professionals who are looking to advance their careers in the financial services sector.
editorial.who_should_take: This retired designation was intended for professionals working in pension administration, annuity product management, and retirement plan operations. It provided a framework for understanding the regulatory and administrative requirements of various tax-sheltered retirement products within the financial services sector.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Because the AAPA is retired and has no successor, there is no preparation strategy for this specific exam. Individuals interested in pension administration should contact LOMA to identify current industry standards and active professional development programs. Knowledge of retirement plan types and regulatory requirements remains relevant for the field, but no study path exists for this legacy credential. Please reach out to LOMA for guidance on modern alternatives that align with your current professional development goals and industry needs.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain focused on the technical features and structural components of annuity products used in retirement planning, providing candidates with an understanding of how these financial vehicles function within the scope of retirement account management and long-term investment strategies.

This domain covered the administrative processes required to maintain and manage retirement contracts effectively, ensuring that professionals understood the lifecycle of plan administration procedures and the documentation required to keep retirement accounts in good standing for all participating plan members.

This domain addressed the tax laws and regulatory frameworks governing pension and annuity plans, helping candidates navigate the rules for tax-sheltered annuities and ensuring that all administrative actions remained in full compliance with the relevant legal and industry-specific regulatory requirements.

This domain focused on the operational aspects of delivering customer service within pension administration, emphasizing the importance of standardized service protocols and effective participant support processes to ensure that all retirement plan beneficiaries received accurate and timely assistance with their accounts.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: The AAPA exam is retired and cannot be scheduled or taken. Candidates should not attempt to register for this exam. Please contact LOMA to inquire about current professional development opportunities and active certification exams that may better suit your career goals.

faq.question_title: How many questions were on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The retired AAPA exam consisted of 100 multiple choice questions. This total count was designed to test a candidate's knowledge across all four domains of the pension administration curriculum before the program was officially discontinued by the organization.

The passing score for the AAPA exam was 70. This threshold was established to ensure that all individuals who earned the designation demonstrated a level of proficiency in the core concepts of retirement planning and pension contract administration.

The exam was a 120-minute, linear assessment. Candidates were required to complete the entire set of questions within this specific duration to be considered for the designation, as the time limit was strictly enforced during the testing process.

faq.question_title: Was there a fee for the exam?
faq.answer_text: The price was $130 per exam, with LOMA member discounts available for those who qualified. Please note that this fee structure is no longer applicable as the exam is retired and is no longer available for registration or purchase.
